subject.title: RFC: Distributed Agent Runtime — separate control plane from agent compute

question: Should OpenClaw pursue a first-class core control-plane/runtime split, or narrow this RFC to smaller lifecycle and execution-backend slices behind the existing gateway?
rationale: The requested design changes core runtime ownership, security boundaries, deployment shape, config surface, and compatibility behavior, and current main plus open related work do not settle that product direction.

options.title: Keep as architecture tracker
options.body: Use this issue to hold the broad control-plane/runtime decision while linked worker-isolation and execution-backend PRs prove narrower slices.

options.title: Narrow to lifecycle commands
options.body: Retarget this issue to per-agent start/stop/restart and move distributed runtime protocol work to a separate maintainer design.

options.title: Defer core split
options.body: Keep distributed orchestration outside core unless a narrower missing core API or security boundary is identified.

recommendation.title: Keep as architecture tracker
recommendation.body: Use this issue to hold the broad control-plane/runtime decision while linked worker-isolation and execution-backend PRs prove narrower slices.

likelyOwner.reason: Most connected to current agent-runtime refactors, gateway work, and the open worker-runtime isolation experiment.
